subject: Nov usage reconciliation & one-time settlement proposal
messages:
From: Erik Stone <erik@aeroflow.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: SaaS Billing <billing@aeroflow.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected Nov overage — need breakdown

Hi Mina,

We just received November's invoice and there's a ~24% overage compared to our forecasted committed capacity. Line item shows a one-time charge labeled 'retro usage reconciliation'. Can you help us understand where the spike came from and whether this is a billing error?

Quick context: we renewed in Sep and bumped committed units by 15% starting Oct 1. We did not expect a retroactive charge of this size. Our finance team wants the usage detail and a proposed settlement (credit or one-time invoice) to close books this week.

Can you send a breakdown of token usage per service and any notes about throttling/fallbacks or model substitutions that might have increased consumption?

Thanks — Erik
Erik Stone
Head of Platform, AeroFlow Labs
erik@aeroflow.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Erik Stone <erik@aeroflow.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, SaaS Billing <billing@aeroflow.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Nov overage — need breakdown

Hi Erik — thanks for flagging this. Sorry for the surprise. I pulled the thread into our billing queue and we started an initial reconciliation.

Top-level summary so you have context while we assemble files:
- We see a cluster of high-throughput jobs on Nov 14–16 tied to a model variant fallback (large-batch rerouting to a compatible variant while the preferred model was being rolled), which increased token counts for a subset of API calls.
- That routing was automatic; the request logs show no unusual request-level token inflation (i.e., prompts were similar), but the compatible variant used a different tokenization and slightly higher per-response tokens.
- We are preparing a per-route, per-day usage CSV and a proposed settlement credit to make this whole thing net-neutral for AeroFlow.

I'll loop in Ben (sales) and Laura (billing) — Ben can propose the customer-facing settlement and Laura will confirm accounting treatment and documentation for your books. Expect the detailed report + proposed credit by EOD Tuesday.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Erik Stone <erik@aeroflow.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, SaaS Billing <billing@aeroflow.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed one-time settlement for Nov retro usage (DF-2024-0842)

Erik — hi, Ben here. Thanks for your patience — we dug into the raw usage and have a customer-friendly proposal.

Summary of what we found:
- Bulk of unexpected tokens came from a routed batch window on Nov 14 02:00–05:30 UTC when the primary model was being migrated to a new quantized shard. Traffic for long-response jobs (avg output + prompt length ~1.6x normal) was temporarily routed to a compatible model with slightly different tokenization.
- Net incremental token count attributable to routing behavior: ~1.9M tokens (across generation endpoints)
- We accept responsibility for the routing fallback and propose a one-time settlement to eliminate the retro usage charge for AeroFlow.

Proposed settlement (customer-facing):
- One-time credit equal to the retro usage charge: $9,450 (applied as a credit against Dec invoice)
- We will issue an official credit memo and send an updated invoice if you prefer a negative invoice line instead.
- Internal note: Redwood will absorb the cost; this will be processed as a contra-revenue credit under DF-2024-0842.

Attached: proposed_settlement_invoice_DF-2024-0842.pdf (pro forma showing credit applied to Dec).

If you confirm, Laura and I will finalize the credit memo and update your billing. If AeroFlow prefers a one-time invoice + payment reversal instead of a credit, we can do that too — tell us which you prefer for your accounting.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Director, Sales — Enterprise
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Office: +1 650-555-0198
Attachments: proposed_settlement_invoice_DF-2024-0842.pdf (PDF, 34KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Erik Stone <erik@aeroflow.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, SaaS Billing <billing@aeroflow.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Reconciliation details + draft credit note

Erik / AeroFlow billing team — attaching the detailed usage export and a draft credit note for your review.

What you'll see in the CSV (usage_report_nov2026.csv): per-day, per-route token counts; the flagged period is Nov 14–16, with the model-variant column showing the temporary variant. The incremental column shows the delta vs. the Oct baseline for the same routes.

Proposed accounting steps if you accept the settlement: 
1) Redwood issues credit note #0842-CR and applies a $9,450 credit to your Dec invoice (or issues an amended Dec invoice with negative line).
2) AeroFlow confirms which document you need for Q4 close (credit memo vs. negative invoice).
3) We simultaneously create an internal incident (RID-2026-1109) and a postmortem; we'll share the postmortem with your technical contact.

Attachments: usage_report_nov2026.csv (CSV, 42KB), credit_note_draft_0842.pdf (PDF, 12KB)

Please confirm by end of day Thursday so we can finalize accounting entries in time for your close. If you'd like the credit applied sooner, let us know and we can schedule it for immediate application.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Manager, Revenue Operations
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: Erik Stone <erik@aeroflow.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nov usage reconciliation & one-time settlement proposal

Mina / Ben / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear breakdown. We reviewed the CSV and the math looks right from our side. AeroFlow accepts the $9,450 credit applied to the Dec invoice.

Requesting two things to close our books: 
- Please issue the formal credit memo (credit_note_draft_0842.pdf looked fine as a draft; we need the final signed copy for our records).
- Share the postmortem (technical incident RID-2026-1109) once available so our SREs can confirm no repeat routing exposure.

Once we have the credit memo, we'll close this on our side. Appreciate the quick ownership here.

— Erik
Erik Stone
Head of Platform, AeroFlow Labs
